note: T14. WRTH 39th ed. (1985, compiled late 1984), Bophuthatswana section: RADIO PULPIT, P.O. Box 3436 Pretoria; STATION Hebron 540 kHz 50 kW; daily programmes to South Africa and Bophuthatswana; on-air ID 'This is Radio Pulpit broadcasting on Radio 540 Bophuthatswana'. So at the end of 1984 Radio Pulpit was on 540 kHz, not 657 kHz. Disagrees with a 657 kHz start in 1981; agrees with a later move to 657. WRTH 1985 prints no 657 kHz entry for South Africa that I could find (OCR).

T14. DX Listening Digest 2005-041 (2005-03-08): a Harare listener quotes Sentech's website, which lists MW from Meyerton: 657 kHz Radio Pulpit (Commercial) and 576 kHz Metro FM (SABC). Secondary but contemporaneous. Earliest source found that places Radio Pulpit on 657 kHz. DXLD 2007-075 (2007-06-30) lists 657 R. Pulpit (gospel), Meyerton (Joburg), 50 kW, among MW stations still on air in July 2007, with 576 R. Metro Meyerton 50 kW. Radio Metro was thus on AM 576 kHz from the same site.

note: T14. The Media Online, 2016-08-11, 'Radio Pulpit 657AM turns 35': the station has been on air since 1981 and celebrated its 35th birthday on 4 August (so 1981-08-04). The article names 657AM as the station's current frequency; it does not say it was on 657 in 1981. WRTH 1985 puts Radio Pulpit on 540 kHz at Hebron, so the likeliest reading (my inference) is that the station began in 1981 and moved to 657 kHz later. Move date not found. Reportedly an ICASA frequency list (PDF, not opened) dates the Meyerton 657 entry 1993-01-01 and a 1999 IBA plan (polity.org.za, HTTP 403) dates it 23 Nov 1978; both look like licence dates and neither is verified here.

note: T11c. The station's own archived home page (capture 1998-06-24): 'SAfm is South Africa's National English Radio station broadcasting in Stereo between 104 and 107 FM' (frequency as printed, no unit; national band range, no city split). The page's hit counter reads 'visitor number since Sept 1996', so the SAfm name was already in use on the station's website from September 1996: circumstantial support for a 1996 name start (agrees with the Africultures 1996-09-28 relaunch row; disagrees with ESAT's 1995), but a counter start date is not a rename date. The page never mentions Radio South Africa. No earlier capture exists (CDX earliest is this one).

note: T11d. 'Writing for the Media in South Africa' (1998), media-history timeline, seen only as archive.org full-text-search snippets (lending-only item): under 1986 it says M-Net 'first goes out on October 1', and the next entry reads 'The SABC introduces Radio Metro, a township English station targeted at Radio Bop's audience'. No month is given for Radio Metro. The entry sits right after the 1 October M-Net start, which may be how 'October 1986' got attached to Radio Metro; that is my inference only. The same timeline says 'Good Hope splits into Good Hope Metro and Radio Kontrei' (year not visible), relevant to the Kfm question.

note: T11a. Not found: a dated primary source for the rename of Radio 5 to 5FM. Bounds from what I could read: still 'Radio 5' in January 1985 (Rand Daily Mail, 1985-01-12) and in WRTH 1985 (compiled late 1984); 'Five FM' used for the station by SABC-derived text about 1986 to 1988 (oldradio page, retrospective); the name '5FM' appears in WRTH 2003 (vol. 57, full-text snippet 'SAFM R.2000 5FM R. Metro'). The year 1992 appears only in Wikipedia's 5FM page (no footnote on that clause, per the T2 file) and in a search-result summary of the same. So 'early 1980s' is refuted, 1992 is unverified, and the true date lies between January 1985 and 2003. WRTH 1986 to 1996 editions are lending-only on archive.org (HTTP 401 or 403) and would settle it.
